summary: A conservative public crosswalk from LawVM assurance statements to specifications, implementations, tests, deployment boundaries, and non-claims reviewed on the snapshot date.
reliance_boundary: This registry describes a dated review of development mechanisms. Repository-relative evidence paths are useful locators but are not bound here to a frozen public release. The registry is not an owner-ratified public schema, legal certificate, external audit, or claim that every frontend has uniform enforcement.

registry_gaps.stable_checker_commands: No stable public checker command is registered. The repository checker remains experimental.
registry_gaps.guard_liveness_index: Relevant failure-path tests are listed among test paths, but no separately owned guard-liveness registry is frozen.
registry_gaps.corpus_witness_ids: Claims are not yet cross-linked to stable, release-bound corpus witness identifiers.
registry_gaps.owner_ratification: No public schema owner or claim-review authority has ratified this registry.
registry_gaps.release_verification: A clean development state was inspected, but no reproducible CI run or last-verified LawVM release is attached to this website review snapshot.
registry_gaps.remote_path_resolution: Evidence paths are repository-relative. The public repository is a moving development surface, so those locators remain externally uncheckable as a dated set until a release-bound archive is published.

mechanism_vocabulary.specified: A normative contract defines the property and its boundary.
mechanism_vocabulary.typed: The phenomenon has explicit carriers and failure or residual states.
mechanism_vocabulary.observe_only: The mechanism records a result but does not uniformly block state promotion.
mechanism_vocabulary.production_blocking: A scoped live lane prevents a candidate state or claim from leaving its seam when the mechanism fails.
mechanism_vocabulary.independently_checked: A separate read-only implementation validates the declared property without calling the producing writer.
mechanism_vocabulary.model_proved: The stated property is proved for a declared mathematical model, not necessarily the production implementation.
mechanism_vocabulary.property_tested: Generated, stateful, metamorphic, or mutation-oriented tests exercise the implementation property.
mechanism_vocabulary.corpus_demonstrated: Pinned real-source witnesses exercise the mechanism within a declared corpus.
mechanism_vocabulary.externally_adjudicated: An external institution or expert accepted or refuted one specific finding.

outcome_vocabulary.established_within_scope: Every declared obligation for this claim and scope is satisfied.
outcome_vocabulary.qualified: The claim depends on named allowances or limitations.
outcome_vocabulary.blocked: A required proof or authority input is missing.
outcome_vocabulary.invalid: Integrity, trace, invariant, or accounting is contradictory.
outcome_vocabulary.uncheckable: A required committed artifact is unavailable.
outcome_vocabulary.not_claimed: The mechanism, operation family, source lane, or conclusion is outside the declared scope.

claims.title: Canonical artifact identity and source lineage
claims.statement: For supported canonical objects and source bundles, LawVM can bind a result to exact artifact identities, availability states, manifestations, units, policies, and domain-separated roots.
claims.scope: Core canonical encoding and substrate source objects; artifact identity only.
claims.deployment: Implemented in the core substrate; frontend source-universe completeness remains profile-specific.
assumptions: The declared source keeper and source role are appropriate for the intended claim.
The bytes supplied to the identity layer are the bytes the caller intends to identify.
claims.allowed_wording: LawVM can identify and rehash the exact canonical artifacts declared by a supported dossier or pack profile.
claims.forbidden_wording: LawVM proves that the source keeper published the complete and legally correct source universe.
known_limits: Integrity does not prove legal correctness, completeness, or source preference.
The public certificate/schema ecosystem is not frozen or owner-ratified.

claims.title: Replay conservation and no silent loss
claims.statement: Within a checked effect universe, each declared source effect must receive an emitted-operation, typed-rejection, or typed-observation disposition, and emitted operations must retain a source warrant.
claims.scope: Core conservation primitive and frontend families that wire it to a declared population.
claims.deployment: Core invariant; production reachability and blocking coverage vary by frontend and operation family.
assumptions: The declared effect universe is itself complete for the scoped check.
Every frontend adapter supplies stable effect identities.
claims.allowed_wording: For a declared checked universe, LawVM tests whether every source effect received a typed disposition.
claims.forbidden_wording: LawVM has proved that every frontend discovers and handles every effect in every source.
known_limits: Conservation cannot prove that a disposition is substantively correct.
A source effect absent from the declared universe cannot be recovered by the partition check.

claims.title: Typed operation closure without silent authority
claims.statement: The core closure boundary returns either a typed closed operation or a blocked candidate carrying residuals; closure itself does not authorize mutation.
claims.scope: Canonical operation closure and phase-local execution-assessment carriers.
claims.deployment: Implemented core boundary; frontend lowering and exact-state admission remain separately scoped.
assumptions: The frontend parser and lowering step supplied the correct typed interpretation.
The active profile names the required closure fields.
claims.allowed_wording: Missing target, payload, source-anchor, or time evidence can remain a blocked typed candidate instead of being guessed.
claims.forbidden_wording: A closed operation proves that the source prose legally entails the operation or grants legal authority.
known_limits: There is no general independent source-language-to-operation entailment checker.
Admission enforcement is not uniform across frontends.

claims.title: Write receipts, independent observation, and mutation boundaries
claims.statement: LawVM has typed write receipts, a before/after observer independent of writer bookkeeping, receipt-totality checks, and mutation-boundary proof carriers.
claims.scope: Core apply-accounting types plus the operation families and profiles that emit and enforce them.
claims.deployment: Mixed. All six apply frontends have observe wiring; selected lanes have block promotion. Receipt production and persistence are not universal.
assumptions: The before and after trees fully represent the checked subject.
The path projection used by the observer captures every relevant mutation.
The declared target and named allowances were established upstream.
claims.allowed_wording: On wired profiles, LawVM can compare declared and independently observed writes and report or block unexplained mutation-boundary disagreement according to the profile.
claims.forbidden_wording: Every LawVM mutation is independently proved correct or production-blocking.
known_limits: The mechanism proves a bounded footprint relation, not that the source instruction justified the operation.
Observe-versus-block behavior and receipt persistence differ by frontend and family.

claims.title: Bounded temporal and occupancy model properties
claims.statement: Z3 harnesses prove named selector and occupancy properties for their encoded finite models, and implementation tests exercise related runtime behavior.
claims.scope: The exact Z3 encodings for two-rail temporal selection, occupancy transitions, and evidence-tier precedence.
claims.deployment: Model evidence plus implementation tests; no end-to-end model-to-Python refinement claim.
assumptions: The encoded model accurately represents the property being discussed.
Jurisdictional commencement and identity rules outside the model remain separate.
claims.allowed_wording: Named temporal and occupancy properties are proved for declared Z3 models and tested against selected implementation behavior.
claims.forbidden_wording: LawVM is formally verified or has proved complete legal-time correctness.
known_limits: The TLA+ model is a finite abstraction and has no full Python refinement proof.
The models do not establish complete jurisdictional commencement doctrine.

claims.title: Experimental independent structural and trace checker
claims.statement: A separate read-only checker implementation can validate canonical roots, internal links, and declared set/delete transition folding for repository fixtures.
claims.scope: Experimental substrate fixtures and the declared structural/transition contract only.
claims.deployment: Experimental repository machinery. No public certificate bundle or stable checker CLI is claimed.
assumptions: The checker implementation and canonical encoding are correct.
The supplied fixture contains the artifacts required by its declared contract.
claims.allowed_wording: The repository contains an experimental checker that independently validates bounded structural and transition-fixture properties.
claims.forbidden_wording: LawVM currently publishes independently checkable legal dossiers or a stable certificate/checker product.
known_limits: The bundle writer is experimental and its fixtures must not be presented as checked legal certificates.
The checker does not independently parse legislative prose or establish source-to-operation entailment.
Public schema ownership, versioning, and release packaging remain unfinished.

claims.title: Live-model import firewall around replay and projection
claims.statement: A repository test computes the replay/projection import cone, rejects edges to fenced live-model clients, and includes a synthetic breach proving that the scanner can fire.
claims.scope: The import roots and fenced client modules declared by the determinism-firewall test.
claims.deployment: Repository enforcement test; AI-assisted proposal and adjudication tools remain permitted outside the declared cone.
assumptions: The declared cone roots and fenced client list remain complete.
Runtime behavior matches the statically inspected imports for this property.
claims.allowed_wording: The declared replay/projection import cone is tested not to import a live model client, and the guard is tested with a synthetic breach.
claims.forbidden_wording: No AI is used anywhere in LawVM or the entire system is free of every form of nondeterminism.
known_limits: The firewall is scoped to declared import roots and clients.
Pinned or reviewed model-generated proposals may exist outside the deterministic replay cone.
